questions.question: Which prefix identifies a class selector in CSS?
questions.explanation: A period prefix (.class-name) designates a class selector in CSS.

questions.question: Which selector matches every single element in the HTML document?
questions.explanation: The asterisk (*) is the universal selector that targets all elements.

questions.question: Which attribute selector targets links whose href attribute ends with '.png'?
questions.hint: $= matches the end of the string.
questions.explanation: The $= operator matches attribute values that end with the specified string.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to use classes instead of IDs for CSS styling?
options: Classes are reusable across multiple elements and have balanced specificity that is easy to override
Browsers only allow 5 IDs per page
questions.explanation: Classes can be reused across any number of elements and have manageable specificity, avoiding hard-to-maintain specificity wars.

questions.question: What does input[type="checkbox"]:checked select?
options: All checkbox inputs that are currently checked/active
The label next to a checkbox
questions.explanation: input[type="checkbox"]:checked targets checkbox elements that are in the checked state.
